description:
The workflow starts with a gene set created from Example gene set. CTD is applied which diffuses through all nodes in STRING[1] to identify nodes that are "guilty by association" and highly connected to the initial gene set of interest[2][3]. A list of Highly Connected Genes was obtained from the CTD output. A list of Guilty By Association Genes was obtained from the CTD output. 
1. Szklarczyk, D. et al. STRING v10: protein–protein interaction networks, integrated over the tree of life. Nucleic Acids Research vol. 43 D447–D452 (2014). doi:10.1093/nar/gku1003
2. Thistlethwaite, L. R. et al. Correction: CTD: An information-theoretic algorithm to interpret sets of metabolomic and transcriptomic perturbations in the context of graphical models. PLOS Computational Biology vol. 17 e1009551 (2021). doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009551
3. Petrosyan, V. et al. Identifying biomarkers of differential chemotherapy response in TNBC patient-derived xenografts with a CTD/WGCNA approach. iScience vol. 26 105799 (2023). doi:10.1016/j.isci.2022.105799
name: Use Case 10: Guilt by Association
tools: extract nodes that are "guilty by association" and connect your initial genes of interest within the graph.
extract nodes that are determined to be highly connected by ctd in your initial node set and display them in a table.
start with a set of genes
use ctd to "connect the dots" and identify highly connected set of proteins in the string protein interaction graph. *please note 10-150 genes of interest are required to run ctd
